Alex: Heads up — saw a tail-p95 regression on dedicated (eu) last night around 03:12 UTC. Correlates with high prefix-cache hit rate for several customer workloads. Suspect batcher/kernel selection interaction when prefill is cached. profiler snapshot attached :eyes:
Maria: Ugh. Any quick logs or profiler traces? which kernel got chosen?
Alex: Paste of runtime log excerpt:
```
[03:12:07] req=0x7f8a kv_cache_hit=true prefix_len=128 suffix_len=24 virtual_len_estimate=24 chosen_kernel=attention_blocked_v2 (slow) alt_kernel=fused_attention_fast (fast) batch_size=3
[03:12:07] req=0x7f9b kv_cache_hit=false prefix_len=128 suffix_len=24 virtual_len_estimate=152 chosen_kernel=fused_attention_fast batch_size=3
```
Seems like when kv_cache_hit=true we report virtual_len as only suffix_len (24) but kernel selector still applies heuristics tuned for full seq. Outcome: smaller reported vlen + cache hits -> micro-batches form but runtime chooses a kernel path that ends up being slower because internal code expects different memory layout.
Chen: That matches a hypothesis I had — token budget and admission logic count suffix tokens differently when prefix is cached. We might be underestimating memory pressure which pushes packing heuristics to overpack heterogeneous requests, then kernel fallback hits because of alignment.
Jonah: Quick mitigation idea: add a kv-cache-aware kernel preference override. If kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.6 or avg_reported_vlen < X but actual_mem_estimate > Y, prefer fused_attention_fast. Also consider token_budget_multiplier=1.25 for cached-prefill workloads so batcher packs fewer suffixes per batch.
Maria: Can we reproduce locally with the seq generator? I can spin a small perf job that toggles kv hits and compares kernel/runtime time.
Alex: I ran a microbench: with 80% kv hits, p95 went from 45ms -> 78ms. Kernel switch count up 4x. Flamegraph showed attention kernel spilled to slower path because of kernel-choice mispred (attached as link to internal trace). :fire:
Sreela: I'll add a trace tag filter and pull samples: `ri-trace query --from=2567880000 --to=2567895000 --filter 'kv_cache_hit:true' --show kernel,virtual_len,chosen_kernel` — should get concrete counts.
OpsBot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for config branch `kv-aware-packer` to pool `dedicated-eu-1` (3 hosts) at 04:30 UTC.
Chen: Proposed patch (sketch):
```
// batcher heuristics: when kv_cache_hit estimated > threshold
if (kv_cache_hit_prob > 0.6) {
  token_budget *= 0.8; // be conservative on suffix packing
  prefer_kernel = KernelPreference::LOW_LATENCY;
  disable_virtual_len_optimistic_mode = true;
}
```
We need AB test with metrics: kernel_switch_rate, p50/p95 latency, batch_size_dist, tokens_per_sec.
Jonah: Agreed on metrics. Also add a gauge for `reported_virtual_len_vs_mem_estimate_ratio` so we can detect mismatch. If ratio < 0.5 often, that's a red flag.
Maria: For rollout plan: 1) feature-flagged patch, 2) 1% canary for 2h, look at p95 and kernel_switch_rate, 3) 10% for 6h, then full. If things go sideways, fallback to old kernel selector.
Alex: I'll open the PR with tests + perf harness config. Tagging @Sreela to add trace queries to the perf dashboard. :thumbsup:
Sreela: On it. I'll also add a sampled trace annotation for `kv_cache_hit` so we can join with kernel profiler later.
Chen: One more note — quantized models seem to exacerbate this because kernel performance delta is larger; include both fp16 and int8 in tests.
Jonah: Good call. Also check model sequence-length buckets (short suffix vs long suffix) — the packing edge cases happen when prefix is huge and suffix tiny.
Alex: Action items:
- Alex: PR with kernel-selector guard + flag (today)
- Maria: run local perf job and post results (today)
- Sreela: add trace queries and dashboard panels (today)
- Chen: expand perf matrix to quantized models (tomorrow)
- Jonah: experiment config for token_budget_multiplier and rollout plan (today)

Alex: Thanks team — will post links to PR and perf artefacts in this thread once available. :rocket:
